newsitem.title: HONG KONG: CRC mulls future Cosmos asset injections.
newsitem.headline: CRC mulls future Cosmos asset injections.

text.p: China Resources (Holdings) Ltd (CRC), said on Tuesday it may inject further machinery businesses into Cosmos Machinery Enterprises Ltd in the future.

"It is possible (there will be) further injection of machinery assets into Cosmos if the opportunity arises," Wang Junqing, general manager of CRC unit China Resources Machinery Co Ltd, a unit of CRC, told a news briefing on Tuesday.
"We will be happy to consider any of these (injection) proposals in future," said Patrick Cheng, executive director of Cosmos Machinery.

CRC, the trading arm of China's Ministry of Foreign Trade and the parent of Hong Kong-listed China Resources Enterprise Ltd, will hold 24.3 percent of Cosmos Machinery on completion of the sale of all its 49 percent stake in Welltec Industrial Equipment Ltd to Cosmos Machinery.

"CRC's investments in machinery will be done through Cosmos, which is able to capitalise on CRC's connections in China in securing further investment opportunities," said Zhu Youlan, vice chairman of CRC.

Cosmos Machinery earlier agreed to buy a 100 percent stake in Welltec from Tai Tung Industrial Equipment Ltd for HK$272.9 million. The purchase would be settled by an issue of 303.22 million new Cosmos Machinery shares at HK$0.90 each.
Tai Tung is 51 percent owned by Cosmos' parent Cosmos Holdings and 49 percent by CRC.
On completion of the deal, Cosmos Holdings' stake in Cosmos Machinery would be reduced to 46 percent from 62.4 percent.
"The acquisition will strengthen the company's existing business," said Tang Kwan, chairman of Cosmos Machinery.
CRC has an annual turnover exceeding US$8 billion and its total assets are worth over US$6 billion.

In accordance with the "CRC Development Program" submitted by Zhu for implementation in the next five years, CRC will strive to double the existing value of both its total and net assets by the year 2000.
